details:
When you source control (Unity Teams, Git, Plastic SCM, ...) an avatar/world project with other users, the world/avatar ID attached to the pipeline descriptor will be checked in too.
However if we allow to use Windows' environment variables, the ID can be decoupled from the project and only the environment variable name must be checked in.
As a result, users can assign the correct value on their dev machine's end instead of hardcoding it into the pipeline component.
Worlds do not allow for shared ownership nor will that solve the problem of having a personal test world before checking in code. This acts against hardcoding the ID.
If the ID is not hardcoded, the mental and manual overhead of adjusting it every time remains.
An environment variable is a special variable scoped to all your applications. You can set them by pressing the Windows key, type "environment variable" in the search (assuming your Windows is English) 
and press "Edit the System Environment Variables".
On the very bottom, you will find the "Environment Variables..." button, click that and you are set to alter your variables.
The implementation for this in VRChat may be as the following:
1. The user selects "raw world ID" or "environment variable" from a drop-down menu.
2. The user types in the name of the environment variable.
3. VRChat, at the time of bundling and building the world, will fetch the ID and place it as serialised ID propery.

The drop-down menu could be ignored if the system parses for a valid ID first and if the format is incorrect, falls back to an environment variable, but this is less predictable or clear on the user end.
title: Allow Environment Variables for World IDs
